Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier 

really helpful. I wanted to capture a short post-call recap and outline the things we need to validate on our side before we commit to a POC. High level our priorities are:

- Auth: we need to evaluate API key vs mTLS for server-to-server calls (data classification requires stronger auth for some endpoints).
- SDK quickstart: sample apps in Python and TypeScript so our backend and frontend teams can iterate locally.
- Routing / fallback: we need predictable routing (latency-first vs cost-first) and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant when capacity is constrained.
- Structured output / tool calling: we want to use tool calling for safe actions and structured output for downstream parsing.
- Embeddings & reranker: vector store integration and guidance on using embeddings + reranker for recommender/ranking flows.

Can you send a short post-call recap + next steps, sample repo links, and any quick environment setup notes (env vars, local testing) we can hand to our engineers?

Hi Tom / Sara,

Great to meet 





thanks for sharing the MVP doc. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. I copied Dev (platform) and Dylan (solutions) to help with the technical follow-up.

Recap (what we covered)
- Auth: Redwood supports API keys and mTLS. For regulated endpoints we recommend mTLS + KMS-backed keys; API keys are fine for lower-sensitivity calls with fine-grained route-level controls.
- SDKs: We have sample quickstart repos for Python and TypeScript (link below). They include local mock servers and example env files.
- Routing & fallback: You can configure routing policies (latency | cost | region) per route; automatic fallback to compatible model variants is available for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
- Structured output & tool calling: SDKs show structured output schemas and tool-calling patterns. We also have an examples folder with a ticket-creation tool calling flow.
- Embeddings & reranker: We recommend embedding at index time and running a light reranker (sequence-level) in the request path for higher precision; included sample for FAISS integration.

Next steps
1) Dev to share a short tech note (env vars, auth, local testing) and example snippets for Python/TS 





target: EOD next business day.
2) Send sample repo + quickstart checklist to your engineers.
3) Schedule a 45-minute technical walkthrough with your backend + infra team next week to deep-dive on mTLS and routing policies.

- Quickstart checklist: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C4d5E6f

Tom / team 


quick technical notes and local testing steps to hand your engineers. TL;DR: Python and TypeScript quickstarts are plug-and-play; for mTLS you'll want to provision certs and enable the client-cert flag in the SDK config.

Auth options (short)
- API keys: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env; scope keys per-route when possible. Good for quickstarts and server-side services.
- mTLS: mutual TLS with certs managed by your infra or Redwood Private. Config: set REDWOOD_MTLS_CERT_PATH and REDWOOD_MTLS_KEY_PATH and enable AUTH_TYPE=mTLS in .env. We recommend KMS for key lifecycle if you need rotation/SOA.

Python quickstart (local)
- Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart && cd sdk-quickstart/python - Copy .env.example -> .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_MTLS_* vars.
- Install: python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt- Run local mock server for testing: python mock_server.py (listens on localhost:8080 and mimics routing/fallback).- Run sample: python samples/chat_demo.py --model redwood-compat/gpt-4o --structured-schema samples/schemas/ticket_v1.json

TypeScript quickstart (local)
- Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart && cd sdk-quickstart/ts - Copy .env.example -> .env and set env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_MTLS_*; also set NODE_ENV=development- Install: npm ci- Start mock server: npm run start:mock- Run sample: node dist/samples/chat_demo.js --model redwood-compat/gpt-4o --tooling-enabled

Routing & fallback notes
- Routing policy is set per-route in routes.yaml. Example: policy: latency_preferred; fallback: model-quantized-v2- For SDK quickstart we include a routes.sample.yaml that demonstrates latency-first vs cost-first configs.

Embeddings & reranker
- Use the embeddings client to upsert vectors at index time. Our samples show FAISS + a lightweight reranker module (python/ts) that reorders the top-K results using a sequence-level scoring call.

Local testing tips
- Use the included mock_server to validate request/response shapes and structured outputs without hitting production.
- Enable verbose logging: REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
- For tool-calling flows, the mock server will emulate tool endpoints; set TOOL_ENDPOINTS in .env to point to local services.

I'll throw these into the quickstart README and create a short gdoc with mTLS checklist and cert examples. Happy to pair on the walkthrough.

- Dev
